issue_context.title: kube-controller-manager memory leak when frequently create and delete same crd
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

 when frequently create and delete same crd, kube controller manager memory leak

throuth golang heap
![pprof](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13744637/203279108-4a0c4e96-4ffc-472e-9dab-a4844f9d5c04.PNG)

when create crd， gc controller will use shared  informer, and add a new event handler to shared informer.
when delete crd， gc controller only close stop chan, and not remove event handler from shared informer
so if frequently  create and delete same crd, leak event handler in shared informer, lead to kcm memory leak.

### What did you expect to happen?

no memory leaks

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

local up a cluster, and execute this script,finally memory usage continue rising

``` bash
#!/bin/bash

export KUBECONFIG=/var/run/kubernetes/admin.kubeconfig
while :
do
    cluster/kubectl.sh create -f crd.yaml
    sleep 30
    cluster/kubectl.sh delete -f crd.yaml
    sleep 30
done
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

Just to add, we have seen this happening not only when CRDs are deleted, but if there is any 'flapping' of discovery lookups (i.e. intermittent failures to do a full discovery lookup).

This leads to ever-increasing workqueue adds for GC and ResourceQuota due to having multiple informer's event handlers registered for the same resource type (gradually growing over time).

I realized there's an existing bug in GC we need to fix before we merge this. If there's a discovery error today, GC drops the monitors for the resources within the group/versions that hit discovery errors. Then when discovery recovers, it readds those monitors, and now has duplicate event handlers.

While we're in a state with discovery errors, we don't actually want to drop existing synced informers for things in that group or we'll miss deletion information when the informer recovers. Fix in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117992
don't add this here, let's find a different way to ensure the cleanup happens
check the result, ErrorS on error, InfoS on success

This removes the event handler but doesn't do anything to clear out the things observed from this API from the GC graph

There are two cases I think we need to handle differently:
* Removal of a CRD: if GC is watching widgets v1beta1, and I delete the widgets v1beta1 API, widget instances should probably get cleared from the graph?
* Addition of a new version to a CRD: if GC is watching widgets v1beta1, and I update the CRD to define a v1 version, that will show up as "start watching v1, stop watching v1beta1". In that case, I think we would want to transition instances in the GC graph to the v1 API, not remove and re-add them.

We need test coverage for both of those cases to make sure we do the right thing.

* Addition of a new version to a CRD: if resource quota is watching widgets v1beta1, and I update the CRD to define a v1 version, that will show up as "start watching v1, stop watching v1beta1". We need test coverage for both of those cases to make sure we do the right thing.
